sec.title: Purpose
sec.p: In East Asia, melanoma mainly presents as the acral lentiginous subtype, followed by the cutaneous subtype. Patients with completely resected stage III or IV melanoma in East Asia are at a high risk of disease recurrence. The adjuvant efficacy of PD-1 inhibitors as monotherapy remains limited in this patient population, underscoring the need for combination strategies.

sec.title: Patients and methods
sec.p: This prospective, single-arm, phase II trial (NCT05907512) aimed to investigate adjuvant recombinant human endostatin (rh-endostatin, an angiogenesis inhibitor) combined with toripalimab (a PD-1 inhibitor) in Chinese patients with resectable stage III to oligometastatic stage IV melanoma. The primary endpoint was 1-year relapse-free survival (RFS). Paired peripheral blood samples before and after the combined adjuvant therapy were collected for single-cell RNA sequencing, TCR/BCR sequencing, and biomarker identification. Two independent real-world cohorts of patients with locally advanced melanoma were assessed to validate the biomarkers.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Forty-three eligible patients with resected stage III melanoma were prospectively enrolled. No patients with resected oligometastatic stage IV disease were enrolled. The 1-year RFS of the patients was 74.4%, with a median RFS of 27 months (95% confidence interval: 19, not reached). Anemia (12/43, 27.9%), elevated liver enzymes (11/43, 25.6%), and thyroid dysfunction (9/43, 20.9%) were the three most common treatment-related adverse events. The combined adjuvant therapy expanded the patients’ peripheral total T and NK cells, increased circulating CD8+ Tem and Teff cells and their TCR clonal diversities, improved the antigen-presenting capacity of B cells, elevated BCR clonal diversity, and raised the number of non-classical monocytes and their antigen-presenting capacity. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and circulating CD8+ Tem cells were supported as candidate biomarkers associated with outcomes in the independent real-world cohorts.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: Adjuvant rh-endostatin combined with toripalimab shows encouraging clinical activity and may be associated with a potential survival benefit in Chinese patients with resected locally advanced melanoma. Adverse reactions were manageable. The increased quantities and functional changes of peripheral T cells, NK cells, B cells, and monocyte subsets provide mechanistic insights for the optimization of immunotherapy.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Melanoma is a malignant tumor arising from melanocytes, with a high tendency for recurrence and metastasis to regional lymph nodes (LNs). The incidence of melanoma varies significantly across countries and regions. The highest incidence rates are reported in Australia and New Zealand, with 42 cases per 100,000 person-years for men and 31 cases per 100,000 person-years for women. Conversely, in most Asian countries, melanoma remains rare, with an incidence usually lower than one case per 100,000 person-years [1, 2]. There are significant differences in melanoma characteristics and treatment strategies between Asian and non-Asian countries. Among Asian populations, acral melanoma—occurring on the palms, soles, and nail beds—is more prevalent. In contrast, among Caucasian populations, cutaneous melanoma constitutes the majority of melanoma cases and is most commonly found in sun-exposed areas such as the head, neck, and trunk. Among Asian patients, acral melanoma is often underdiagnosed and typically identified at an advanced stage, which contributes to an unfavorable prognosis. By contrast, in Western countries, cutaneous melanoma is more frequently detected at an early stage, resulting in a more favorable prognosis [3, 4].

Even after complete resection of the primary lesion and sentinel lymph node biopsy with or without regional lymph node dissection, locally advanced melanoma still carries a high risk of local recurrence and distant metastasis. In Western countries, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), e.g., programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) monoclonal antibodies, are the standard adjuvant treatment, demonstrating remarkable efficacy [5, 6]. However, in Asian patients, the response rate of melanoma to ICI monotherapy remains relatively low, requiring the combination of anti-angiogenic drugs or the exploration of novel immunotherapeutic strategies. Therefore, this study proposed an innovative combined treatment involving toripalimab (a PD-1 inhibitor) and recombinant human endostatin (rh-endostatin, an angiogenesis inhibitor) as adjuvant therapy in Chinese patients with resectable stage III or IV melanoma. This study aimed to reduce the risk of postoperative recurrence in these patients and to identify potential prognostic biomarkers.

sec.title: Trial design, participants and sample size
sec.p: This was an exploratory prospective, single-center, single-arm, phase 2 clinical trial (registration number: NCT05907512). The inclusion criteria for this trial were as follows: a diagnosis of acral or cutaneous melanoma, confirmed by surgical and/or biopsy pathology (excluding mucosal or uveal melanoma); patient age ≥ 18 years; an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 0 or 1; and completely resected stage III or oligometastatic stage IV melanoma. Disease stage was determined based on the melanoma staging system of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) [7]. Furthermore, patients must have received no prior adjuvant anti-melanoma treatment. The exclusion criteria were as follows: autoimmune disorders (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, autoimmune thyroid diseases and inflammatory bowel disease); a requirement for the long-term administration of glucocorticoids or immunosuppressive agents; and a concurrent diagnosis of other malignant tumors.

The sample size was estimated based on the 1-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) rate of 61.0% in patients with completely resected locally advanced melanoma who did not receive adjuvant therapy [5]. We estimated that the combined adjuvant therapy could increase the 1-year RFS rate to 81.0%. The sample size was calculated using PASS software, version 15.0. At a two-sided significance level of α = 0.05 and a power of 0.80, a total of 43 subjects needed to be enrolled. This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (approval number: 2009224-4-2304B). All participants provided written informed consent.

sec.title: Treatment, follow-up and endpoints
sec.p: The participants initiated adjuvant drug therapy within 13 weeks following complete resection of both the primary and lymph node metastatic lesions. Toripalimab was administered intravenously to patients at 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks in a 4-week cycle (days 1 and 15 of each cycle), for up to 13 cycles or until disease recurrence, unacceptable toxicity or death. Rh-endostatin (Endostar) was administered intravenously at a dose of 210 mg from day 1 to day 3 of each 4-week cycle, for up to 6 cycles or until disease recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or death. Treatment interruption and discontinuation were allowed in the event of unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or protocol violation. Participants’ age, sex, ECOG performance status, melanoma subtype, and B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase (BRAF) mutation status were recorded.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and ultrasound of the pelvic cavity or axilla were conducted every 8 weeks to monitor regional lymph node metastasis. Chest computed tomography (CT), abdominal ultrasound, and brain MRI were conducted to monitor distant organ metastasis. The time of disease relapse, occurrence of adverse events, and survival status were recorded. The primary endpoint was the 1-year RFS rate. RFS was defined as the interval from the initial intravenous administration to the first documented melanoma relapse at any anatomical site (including local recurrence or distant metastasis) or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. Secondary endpoints included distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) and safety outcomes. Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were systematically recorded and classified from grades 0 to 5 in accordance with the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0 [8].

sec.title: Sample collection, sequencing, and library construction
sec.p: Peripheral venous blood (approximately 10 mL) was collected on the day before initiating combined adjuvant therapy and on the first day after the completion of the first cycle of treatment. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated via density gradient centrifugation for sequencing by Singleron Biotechnologies (Nanjing, China). Single-cell suspensions at a concentration of 1 × 10⁵ cells/mL were prepared and loaded into the microfluidic device. Subsequently, scTCR-seq/scBCR-seq libraries were constructed following the protocol of the GEXSCOPE® Single Cell Human V(D)J Kit (Singleron Biotechnologies). In brief, magnetic beads carrying molecular labels captured the poly(A) tails and the T-cell receptor (TCR) regions of mRNA, thereby labeling the cells and mRNA after cell lysis. The magnetic beads within the chip were then collected, and the mRNA captured by these beads was reverse transcribed into complementary DNA (cDNA) and amplified. Sequencing libraries compatible with the Illumina sequencing platform were constructed following fragmentation and splicing of partial cDNA. The remaining cDNA was enriched for immune receptors (TCR/B-cell receptor, BCR), and the enriched products were subsequently amplified by PCR to generate a sequencing library compatible with the Illumina sequencing platform. Finally, each library was sequenced using the Illumina HiSeq X platform with 150-bp paired-end reads.

sec.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) read alignment and quantification
sec.p: Raw reads were processed to generate gene expression profiles using CeleScope v1.5.2 (Singleron Biotechnologies) with default parameters. Cell barcodes and unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) were extracted from R1 reads and subsequently corrected. Adapter sequences and poly(A) tails were trimmed from R2 reads, and the trimmed R2 reads were aligned to the GRCh38 (hg38) transcriptome using STAR v2.6.1b. Uniquely mapped reads were subsequently assigned to exons using FeatureCounts v2.0.1. Successfully assigned reads sharing the same cell barcode, UMI, and gene annotation were grouped to construct a gene expression matrix for downstream analysis.

sec.title: Quality control and dimensionality reduction for scRNA-seq data
sec.p: Scanpy version 1.8.1 was employed to perform quality control, dimensionality reduction, and clustering within the Python 3.7 environment [9]. For each sample dataset, the expression matrix was filtered based on the following criteria: (1) cells with a gene count below 200 or in the top 2% of gene counts were excluded; (2) cells with a UMI count in the top 2% were excluded; (3) genes expressed in fewer than 5 cells were excluded; and (4) cells with a mitochondrial gene content greater than 10% were excluded. Following the filtering process, a total of 95,466 cells were retained for downstream analysis, with an average of 1,120 genes and 2,612 UMIs per cell. The raw count matrix was normalized by the total count per cell and subsequently log-transformed to generate the normalized data matrix. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected. Principal component analysis (PCA) was conducted on the scaled variable gene matrix, and the top 15 principal components were utilized for clustering and dimensionality reduction. Cells were partitioned into 23 clusters using the Louvain algorithm with the resolution parameter set to 1.2. Cell clusters were visualized using Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP). Batch effects across samples were corrected with Harmony version 1.0 [10]. To mitigate the impact of RNA contamination and doublets on downstream analysis, DecontX [11] was employed to estimate and remove contamination, while DoubletFinder [12] was utilized to identify and eliminate doublets.

sec.title: Cell type annotation
sec.p: Cell-ID is a multivariate computational approach that identifies gene signatures at the single-cell level and performs cell identity recognition through hypergeometric testing (HGT). In this study, HGT was performed on these extracted gene signatures against the brain reference from the SynEcoSys™ database (Singleron Biotechnologies), which contains a comprehensive collection of canonical cell type markers for single-cell sequencing data, sourced from CellMakerDB and PanglaoDB. For cluster annotation, the frequency of each cell type was determined within each cluster, and the cell type with the highest frequency was assigned as the cluster’s identity [13]. Furthermore, the annotations were validated based on the expression levels of canonical markers from the reference database SynEcoSys.

sec.title: Differentially Expressed Gene (DEG) analysis
sec.p: We utilized the scanpy.tl.rank_genes_groups function based on the Wilcoxon rank-sum test to identify DEGs. Genes were selected as DEGs if expressed in more than 10% of cells in either of the compared cell groups, with an average log(Fold Change) above 1. Adjusted P-values were obtained using the Benjamini-Hochberg correction. A threshold of 0.05 was applied as the criterion for assessing statistical significance.

sec.title: Pathway enrichment analysis
sec.p: To investigate the potential functions of a specific gene set, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis was conducted using the clusterProfiler R package version 3.16.1 [14]. Pathways with an adjusted P-value below 0.05 were deemed significantly enriched. Significantly enriched pathways were visualized as bar plots. For gene set variation analysis (GSVA), the average gene expression of each cell type was used as input data [15].

sec.title: Pseudotime trajectory analysis and RNA velocity
sec.p: The cell differentiation trajectory was reconstructed using Monocle 2 v2.10.0 [16]. For trajectory construction, the top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected using the FindVariableFeatures function in Seurat (v3.1.2). Dimensionality reduction was performed using the DDRTree function. The trajectory was visualized using the plot_cell_trajectory function in Monocle 2.

For RNA velocity analysis, BAM files containing CD8+ T cells and the reference genome GRCh38 (hg38) were processed using velocyto (v0.2.3) and scVelo (v0.17.17) in Python [17]. The results were projected onto the UMAP plot derived from the Seurat clustering analysis to ensure visualization consistency.

sec.title: Trajectory switch gene analysis
sec.p: Switch gene analysis was conducted using GeneSwitches (v0.1.0) in R version 3.6.3 to identify the temporal order of gene expression and the functional roles of these genes during cell state transitions. For genes exhibiting a distinct bimodal “on-off” distribution, logistic regression was applied to model their binary expression states along pseudotime. The switching point was defined as the time point at which the fitted curve crossed the 0.5 probability threshold. Top switch genes with high McFadden’s Pseudo R² values were visualized using the plot_timeline_ggplot function [18].

sec.title: UCell gene set scoring
sec.p: Gene set scoring was performed using the R package UCell (v1.1.0) [19]. The UCell scoring method is based on the Mann-Whitney U statistic, which ranks query genes according to their expression levels in individual cells. As a rank-based scoring approach, UCell is particularly well-suited for large-scale datasets comprising multiple samples and batches.

sec.title: Transcription Factor (TF) analysis
sec.p: TF analysis was conducted using pySCENIC (v0.11.0) with the scRNA-seq expression matrix and transcription factors sourced from AnimalTFDB. First, GRNBoost2 was utilized to predict a regulatory network based on the co-expression of regulators and their target genes. Subsequently, cisTarget was applied to eliminate indirect targets and identify TF binding motifs. Next, AUCell was employed to quantify regulon activity in individual cells. Cluster-specific TF regulons were determined based on regulon specificity scores (RSSs), and the activity of these regulons was visualized using heatmaps [20].

sec.title: TCR and BCR analysis
sec.p: TCR/BCR clonotype assignment was performed using the CeleScope (v1.15.0) VDJ pipeline with GRCh38 as the reference. For TCR analysis, only cells containing a single productive TCR α-chain (TRA) and a single productive TCR β-chain (TRB) were retained for downstream analysis. For BCR analysis, cells with one productive IGH chain and one productive IGK or IGL chain were included in subsequent analyses. Following clonotype assignment and filtering, V(D)J information was mapped to the single-cell transcriptome data based on the cell barcodes. Each unique TRA(s)-TRB(s) pair was defined as a TCR clonotype, and each unique IGH-IGK/IGL pair as a BCR clonotype.

If a clonotype was present in at least two cells, cells harboring this clonotype were considered clonal, and the number of cells with such pairs indicated the degree of clonality for that clonotype. Clonotype frequency statistics were calculated by group, based on the number of cells expressing each clonotype. Clonotypes with a frequency of 1 were classified as “Single”, those with a frequency ranging from 2 to 10 as “Medium”, and those with a frequency greater than 10 as “Large”. Diversity analysis based on sample clonotype information was performed using the immunarch package. Data visualization was conducted using ggplot2 (v3.5.1), pheatmap (v1.0.12), ComplexHeatmap (v2.14.0) in R. Statistical tests for diversity indices were performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and adjustments for multiple comparisons were performed using the Holm method.

sec.title: Cell-cell communication analysis
sec.p: Cell-cell communication among cell types was predicted based on known ligand–receptor pairs with CellphoneDB(v2.1.0) [21]. CellphoneDB integrates a database of ligands, receptors, and their interactions. The number of cells was restricted to 500 for each cell type for analysis. If the total number of cells was below 500, the entire observed cell count was retained. To establish the null distribution of average ligand–receptor pair expression under randomized cell identity assignments, we set the number of permutations to 1000. Cell type–specific expression thresholds for ligands and receptors were defined based on the distribution of mean log-normalized expression values across all expressed genes within each cell type. Predicted interaction pairs with a P value < 0.05 and an average log expression > 0.1 were considered significant. The interactions were visualized via heatmap_plot and dot_plot in Cellphone DB.

sec.title: Real-world melanoma cohorts for validation
sec.p: To evaluate the prognostic significance of neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in patients with locally advanced melanoma, we retrospectively enrolled patients with stage III melanoma who underwent complete surgical resection at the Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center between January 2016 and January 2024. The inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) acral or cutaneous melanoma with a confirmed pathological diagnosis; (2) presence of regional LN metastasis, such as axillary, inguinal and/or iliac LN metastasis; and (3) complete resection of both the primary lesion and all involved LN metastases. The exclusion criteria were: (1) incomplete or unavailable survival data; and (2) absence of preoperative complete blood count results in the electronic medical records. Patients’ age, gender, body mass index (BMI), tumor subtype, Breslow thickness, BRAF mutation status, presence of ulceration, and preoperative peripheral blood levels of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) were recorded. RFS and melanoma-specific survival (MSS) were assessed until August 2025. This cohort was designated as Real-world Melanoma Cohort 1.

To explore the prognostic value of circulating CD8+ effector memory T cells (Tem), we included 47 patients with stage III melanoma who underwent surgical resection at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (FUSCC) from April 2023 to November 2024. All patients were tested for CD8+ Tem levels in peripheral blood using flow cytometry before surgical resection. Peripheral blood CD8+ Tem cells were identified by the marker panel CD3+ CD8+ CCR7− CD45RA−. This cohort was designated as Real-world Melanoma Cohort 2.

sec.title: Statistical analysis
sec.p: Statistical analyses were conducted with GraphPad Prism version 9.5 and IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. Continuous variables were expressed as median (quartile) or mean ± standard deviation (SD). Categorical variables were presented as frequencies and percentages. The X-Tile software (version 3.6.1) was used to determine the optimal cutoff value for continuous variables such as NLR. X-Tile is a publicly available bioinformatics software tool, mainly used for identifying the optimal cut-off value most relevant to survival outcomes. X-Tile is used to determine the optimal prognostic cut-point for continuous biomarker variables by maximizing statistical significance in Kaplan–Meier survival stratification. Survival curves were generated by the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. A multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression model was used to identify independent prognostic factors and determine the hazard ratio (HR) with the 95% confidence interval (CI). A P value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

sec.title: Efficacy and safety
sec.p: The study flowchart is presented in Fig. 1A. Between October 2021 and December 2023, 43 eligible patients were prospectively enrolled and assigned to receive the combined adjuvant therapy. Follow-up was maintained until June 15, 2025. The demographic characteristics of the trial participants are summarized in Fig. 1B. Although the protocol allowed for the inclusion of patients with oligometastatic stage IV disease, no such cases were ultimately enrolled, which might be due to a low patient acceptance rate for the radical resection of both the primary and distant organ metastatic lesions among this subgroup. Consequently, the final study cohort consisted entirely of patients with stage III melanoma.

sec.p: Regarding therapeutic efficacy, the 1-year RFS was 74.4%, with a median RFS of 27 months (95% CI: 19, not reached) (Fig. 1C); the 1-year DMFS was 83.1%, and the median DMFS was not reached (Fig. 1D); the 1-year overall survival (OS) was 97.6%, and the median OS was immature (Fig. 1E).

A total of 35 patients (35/43, 81.4%) experienced at least one TRAE, while 8 (18.6%) experienced no TRAEs. Anemia (12/43, 27.9%), elevated liver enzymes (11/43, 25.6%), and thyroid dysfunction (9/43, 20.9%) were the three most common TRAEs (Table S1, Fig. 1F).

A total of seven cases of grade 3 TRAEs occurred (Table S1), including moderate anemia (n = 1), which was relieved after treatment with erythropoietin combined with intravenous iron; elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT, n = 1), which resolved after treatment with glycyrrhizin; hypothyroidism (n = 2), which improved after replacement therapy with levothyroxine sodium (L-T4); rash (n = 1), which subsided after topical application of potent glucocorticoid cream; neutropenia (n = 1), which returned to normal after subcutaneous injection of recombinant human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor; and acute kidney injury (n = 1, manifested as elevated serum creatinine), which resolved after oral prednisone treatment. All grade 3 TRAEs resolved after symptomatic intervention, and the patients successfully resumed subsequent treatment after a brief suspension of the adjuvant therapy.

Two patients experienced grade 4 TRAEs and subsequently discontinued the adjuvant therapy—one due to myocarditis and the other due to renal impairment (Fig. 1G). After two cycles of the adjuvant therapy, patient P35 had cardiovascular symptoms of palpitations and chest pain. Peripheral blood tests showed an elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T concentration of 0.363 ng/mL. Echocardiography indicated a new pericardial effusion. Given the above clinical and imaging evidence, immune-related myocarditis was highly suspected. Toripalimab and rh-endostatin were immediately discontinued and glucocorticoid pulse therapy was initiated. Following a two-week course of symptomatic therapy, the patient exhibited significant improvement in myocarditis-associated clinical manifestations, and the overall clinical condition stabilized. After three cycles of the adjuvant therapy, patient P40 developed massive proteinuria and hypoproteinemia, leading to the cessation of adjuvant treatment. Subsequently, glucocorticoid therapy and intravenous infusions of human albumin were administered. The clinical symptoms related to renal function were significantly relieved.

sec.title: Effect of adjuvant combined therapy on peripheral immune cell landscape
sec.p: A total of 14 paired blood samples obtained from 7 patients before and after the adjuvant combined therapy were collected and sequenced. After quality control (Figure S1A), a total of 95,466 cells were identified, representing 8 cell types: plasma cells, B cells, T and natural killer (NK) cells, neutrophils, basophils, mononuclear phagocytes (MPs), plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs), and erythrocytes (Fig. 2A). The sample origins (Fig. 2B) and group assignments (Fig. 2C) of these cells were recorded. The canonical marker genes for identifying these cell types are presented in Fig. 2D. The top 10 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) for each cell type were identified (Figure S1B).

sec.p: A change in the proportion of immune cells exceeding ± 10% relative to the baseline was defined as either an increase or a decrease. Overall, compared with pre-treatment levels, the proportion of neutrophils decreased, whereas that of lymphocytes (including T cells and NK cells) increased following the treatment (Fig. 2E and Figure S1C). The proportions of T and NK cells increased after the treatment in patients P34, P35, P37, and P40, whereas no such increase was noted in patients P36, P38, and P39 (Fig. 2F). The median RFS of patients with increased T and NK cell levels (P34, P35, P37, and P40) was 14.5 months, versus 8 months for those with decreased levels (P36, P38, and P39) (Fig. 2G). This might indicate a potential association between increased proportions of peripheral blood lymphocytes and therapeutic efficacy.

sec.title: Prognostic value of NLR in resected locally advanced melanoma
sec.p: We further explored the prognostic value of neutrophil, lymphocyte and NLR levels in resected locally advanced melanoma based on a large-scale real-world Chinese melanoma cohort. We retrospectively included patients with stage III melanoma who underwent complete surgical resection of both the primary tumor and regional lymph node metastases at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center from January 2016 to January 2024. A total of 384 patients with resected stage III melanoma were enrolled (Real-world Melanoma Cohort 1). Their baseline and clinical characteristics are presented in Table S2.

In the univariate Kaplan-Meier curve analysis, age, subtype, gene mutation, and ulceration were significantly associated with MSS in patients with resected stage III melanoma (Fig. 2H). High preoperative neutrophil and low preoperative lymphocyte levels were significantly associated with poor MSS (Figure S1D and E). The X-Tile software revealed an optimal prognostic cut-off value of 1.6 for the NLR, and this threshold could best distinguish patient subgroups with different survival outcomes (Figure S1F). Patients with a high preoperative NLR phenotype (> 1.6) showed a shorter MSS compared to those with a low NLR phenotype (≤ 1.6) (Fig. 2H). In the multivariate Cox regression analysis, an optimal NLR > 1.6 was independently associated with poor MSS in patients with resected stage III melanoma (Fig. 2I). Moreover, patients exhibiting a high preoperative NLR demonstrated a significantly shorter RFS compared with those showing a low preoperative NLR (Figure S1G), with an HR of 1.708 (95% CI = 1.261–2.313).

Based on the above single-cell results, adjuvant combined therapy in this study reduced the proportion of neutrophils and increased the proportions of T and NK lymphocytes, which are expected to convert the high NLR phenotype to a low NLR phenotype. These changes may be associated with the survival benefits observed in melanoma patients.

sec.title: Effect of adjuvant combined therapy on T and NK subsets
sec.p: A total of 29,426 T and NK cells were obtained, and detailed annotation identified 11 different subtypes, including CD4+ central memory T cells (CD4Tcm), CD4+ memory T cells (CD4Tmem), CD4+ naive T cells (CD4NaiveT), CD8+ effector T cells (CD8Teff), CD8 + effector memory T cells (CD8Tem), CD8+ exhausted T cells (CD8Tex), CD8+ mucosal-associated invariant T cells (CD8MAIT), CD8+ naive T cells (CD8NaiveT), NK cells, proliferating T cells (Proliferating T) and regulatory T cells (Treg) (Fig. 3A). The top 3 marker genes for each cell type are displayed in Fig. 3B. Overall, adjuvant combined therapy increased the proportions of CD8+ Teff, CD8+ Tem and NK cells (Fig. 3C). The interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) expression score of NK cells was increased after adjuvant combined therapy (Fig. 3D). Moreover, adjuvant combined therapy enhanced the cytotoxicity of CD8+ Tem and NK cells (Fig. 3E).

sec.p: KEGG pathway enrichment analysis was performed on the DEGs of CD8+ Teff before and after adjuvant combined therapy. The adjuvant therapy upregulated signaling pathways related to the natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity in CD8+ Teff cells (Figure S2A). Similarly, the adjuvant therapy upregulated signaling pathways related to the ribosome, antigen processing and presentation, and natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity in CD8+ Tem cells (Figure S2B); the adjuvant therapy upregulated signaling pathways related to the cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, chemokine signaling pathway, natural killer cell mediated cytotoxicity, NF-kappa B signaling pathway, and endocytosis in NK cells (Figure S2C). GSVA pathway enrichment analysis was performed on the DEGs of T cell subsets to investigate functional alterations before and after adjuvant combined therapy (Figure S2D).

Pseudo-temporal analysis indicated that CD8+ Tem and CD8+ Teff were at the terminal stage of differentiation, along the developmental pathway originating from CD8+ Naïve T (Fig. 3F). RNA velocity analysis indicated that CD8+ Tem differentiated into CD8+ Teff (Fig. 3G), thereby exerting anti-tumor immune effects. The switch genes (Figure S2E) and transcription factors (Figure S2F) involved in this differentiation process were identified.

sec.title: Prognostic value of CD8+ Tem
sec.p: To investigate whether CD8+ Tem could serve as a biomarker for the efficacy of adjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy in resected locally advanced melanoma, we included 47 patients with stage III melanoma who underwent radical resection at FUSCC from April 2023 to November 2024 (Real-world Melanoma Cohort 2). All patients had preoperative measurements of peripheral blood CD8+ Tem levels and received adjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy based on routine clinical practice. CD8+ Tem levels (%) were expressed as the percentage of the absolute count of CD8+ Tem cells relative to the total absolute count of CD8+ T cells. Follow-up was conducted until August 2025. The baseline characteristics are presented in Table S3.

Regarding the cutoff rationale for the CD8+ Tem cohort, we used the median value of 40.7% for the entire cohort to dichotomize patients into the high and low groups. This approach ensures that both subgroups contain a comparable number of cases (approximately half of the cohort), which provides balanced sample sizes and optimizes statistical power for detecting differences. Based on the cutoff of 40.7%, which was the median value of CD8Tem for the entire cohort, patients were divided into the CD8Tem_high (≥ 40.7) group (N = 24) and the CD8Tem_low (< 40.7) group (N = 23). As analyzed by the unadjusted Kaplan-Meier method, patients with high CD8Tem exhibited significantly favorable 1-year RFS (87.1% vs. 58.0%) and 2-year RFS (74.5% vs. 32.6%) versus the low CD8Tem group (Fig. 3H).

sec.title: Effect of adjuvant combined therapy on T Cell Receptor (TCR) repertoire
sec.p: The adjuvant combined therapy increased the frequency of the large TCR clonotype (Fig. 4A). Patient P40 with the highest frequency of the large clonotype after treatment (Fig. 4B) clinically demonstrated the best RFS of over 21 months (Fig. 2G). This might indicate that the increase in the frequency of the large TCR clonotype could be another potential mechanism underlying the efficacy of adjuvant combined therapy.

sec.p: In terms of T cell subtypes, the increased frequency of the large TCR clonotype was mainly observed in CD8Tem and CD8Teff (Fig. 4C). The adjuvant therapy increased TCR clonal diversity as measured by the Chao1 index (Fig. 4D) and the D50 index (Fig. 4E).

The number of shared TCR clonotypes among T-cell subtypes after treatment (Fig. 4F) was elevated compared to pretreatment values (Fig. 4G). In particular, the number of shared TCR clonotypes between CD8Tem and CD8Teff after treatment (n = 61) was greater than that found before treatment (n = 54).

Adjuvant therapy increased the usage frequencies of the V genes TRAV12-2 and TRAV20, and the J gene TRAJ42 of the α chain of CD8Tem TCR (Fig. 4H). Similarly, adjuvant therapy increased the usage frequency of the J gene TRBJ1-1 of the β chain of CD8Tem TCR (Figure S3).

sec.p: B cells were divided into five distinct subgroups, including naïve B, switched memory B, unswitched memory B, plasma cells_1, and plasma cells_2 (Fig. 5A). The top 3 marker genes of each cell type are displayed in Fig. 5B.

sec.p: Adjuvant therapy did not elevate the proportion of switched or unswitched memory B cells (Fig. 5C). Nonetheless, adjuvant therapy enhanced the antigen-presenting ability of naïve B, and switched and unswitched memory B cells (Fig. 5D).

Pseudo-temporal analysis revealed that naive B cells differentiated into either switched/unswitched memory B cells or into plasma cells_1 and plasma cells_2 (Fig. 5E). The adjuvant combined therapy increased BCR clonal diversity as measured by the Chao1 index, D50 diversity, Hill numbers and inverse Simpson index (Fig. 5F).

The number of shared BCR clonotypes between B-cell subtypes after treatment (Fig. 5G) was elevated compared to pretreatment (Fig. 5H). In particular, the number of shared BCR clonotypes between naive B and unswitched memory B cells after treatment (n = 39) was greater than that recorded before treatment (n = 21). The number of shared BCR clonotypes between naive B and switched memory B cells after treatment (n = 28) was also greater than the pretreatment value (n = 14).
Adjuvant therapy increased the gene usage frequencies of IGKV3-20, IGKV1-39 (Fig. 5I), IGKJ1 (Fig. 5J) and IGHV4-59 (Fig. 5K) of the BCR.

sec.title: Effect of adjuvant combined therapy on monocytes and dendritic cells
sec.p: Classical monocytes (ClassicalMono), non-classical monocytes (NonClassicalMono) and classical dendritic cells (cDCs) were identified in the MPs system (Fig. 6A). The top 3 marker genes for each cell type are displayed in Fig. 6B. Adjuvant therapy increased the proportion of non-classical monocytes (Fig. 6C). Adjuvant therapy also enhanced the antigen-presenting ability of both classical and non-classical monocytes (Fig. 6D).

sec.title: Cell communications before and after adjuvant therapy
sec.p: The number of interactions of non-classical monocytes on CD8+ Tem, CD8+ Teff and NK cells was greater after treatment versus pretreatment (Fig. 6E). The number of interactions of classical monocytes on CD8+ Tem, CD8+ Teff and NK cells was also greater after treatment than before treatment (Fig. 6F). The number of interactions of cDCs on CD8+ Tem and NK cells after treatment was greater than that found before treatment (Fig. 6G).

Adjuvant therapy enhanced the interactions between CCL3, CCL4, and CCL5 ligands and the CCR5 receptor on CD8+ Teff (Fig. 6H). This signal could facilitate the migration of Teff cells to sites of inflammation or tumor development [22]. Adjuvant therapy enhanced the interaction between CXCL8 ligand (IL-8) and the CXCR2 receptor on NK (Fig. 6I). CXCL8 plays a key role in NK cell-mediated anti-tumor immune responses [23].

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Anti-angiogenic therapy promotes the normalization of blood vessels, improves blood perfusion in tumor tissues, alleviates hypoxia, and thereby facilitates the infiltration of immune cells, synergistically enhancing the efficacy of immunotherapy [24, 25]. Combination immunotherapy with anti-angiogenic agents represents a highly promising therapeutic strategy in melanoma, such as pembrolizumab combined with bevacizumab [26]. Clinical evidence supports the superior efficacy and manageable safety of this combination therapy compared to monotherapy across multiple challenging clinical settings, including advanced or refractory disease subtypes (e.g., mucosal, acral, and melanoma with brain metastases) [27–29].

Toripalimab is a recombinant humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody. It can strongly bind to the PD-1 receptor on the surface of T cells, effectively inhibiting the interaction between PD-1 and PD-L1. Following binding, toripalimab dissociates at a slow rate, thereby conferring a prolonged duration of action. Moreover, toripalimab induces the endocytosis of the PD-1 receptors on T cells, reducing their expression levels on the cell membrane, which more effectively restores the function of T cells [30, 31]. Toripalimab has been proven to achieve highly effective and long-lasting melanoma suppression in Chinese patients with advanced melanoma, especially the acral subtype [32, 33].

Endostar is a modified recombinant human endostatin (rh-endostatin) [34]. Angiogenic factors in the tumor microenvironment, such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF-2), platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF), and angiopoietin (ANGPT), are mainly produced and secreted by tumor cells and stromal cells, leading to enhanced angiogenesis and promoting tumor recurrence and distant metastasis [35]. Preclinical in vivo and in vitro experiments have demonstrated that Endostar inhibits melanoma tumor growth through the suppression of FGF-2-mediated angiogenesis [36]. A clinical trial demonstrated that adding Endostar to dacarbazine can further prolong survival in Chinese patients with metastatic melanoma [37]. The combination of an anti-angiogenic agent and immunotherapy is a new exploration direction in the postoperative adjuvant treatment field for locally advanced acral and cutaneous melanoma patients in East Asia.

In this prospective trial, the 1-year RFS rate for adjuvant toripalimab combined with Endostar after surgery was 74.4%, with a median RFS of 27 months. Although the primary endpoint was not met, because the observed efficacy was numerically lower than the initially hypothesized 1-year RFS rate of 81%, the survival benefit conferred by this combination therapy is promising. This is supported by retrospective historical data from our center, which showed limited efficacy for conventional treatments, such as interferon adjuvant therapy or observation alone (1-year RFS: 45.3–59.2%; median RFS: 13 months) [38].

The combination of an anti-angiogenic agent and a PD-1 inhibitor has the potential synergistic effect in inhibiting melanoma recurrence. Anti-angiogenic agents can normalize tumor vasculature and improve blood perfusion to relapsed tumor lesions, thereby enhancing the distribution and efficacy of PD-1 inhibitors in the tumor microenvironment. It was reported that PD-1 blockade combined with Endostar can exert a synergistic effect through PI3K/AKT/mTOR-mediated autophagy and angiogenesis pathways and suppress tumor growth in LLC mouse models [39].

The combination of PD-1 inhibitors and anti-angiogenic agents may elevate the risk of certain adverse reactions, including proteinuria and immune-related adverse events. In this trial, anemia, elevated liver enzymes and thyroid dysfunction were the three most common TRAEs. In total, 94.3% (33/35) of patients with TRAEs could be effectively managed. According to our findings, myocarditis and proteinuria require particular attention during the course of combined treatment. Appropriate interventions should be implemented promptly.

By collecting paired blood samples before and after adjuvant therapy, we systematically explored the immune mechanisms involved in this combination therapy. We observed that the combination of toripalimab and Endostar could induce multiple beneficial alterations in the peripheral immune microenvironment. First, combined adjuvant therapy increased the overall proportion of circulating lymphocytes and the proportions of NK cells, CD8+ Tem cells and CD8+ Teff cells. A previous single-cell study by Li and colleagues [40] suggested that acral melanoma is characterized by lower overall lymphocyte infiltration and decreased levels of CD8+ Teff cells and NK cells, compared to non-acral cutaneous melanoma. These weak immunological features may contribute to the limited efficacy of anti-PD-1 monotherapy in acral melanoma. Our combined adjuvant therapy may help improve these immune features and could contribute to the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Current evidence indicates that NK cells play a crucial role in the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors independently of cytotoxic T-cell responses [41, 42]. Our combined adjuvant therapy not only increased the number of NK cells and their cytotoxic activity but also enhanced interferon expression in NK cells. Interferon plays a crucial role in enhancing the ability of the immune system to recognize and eliminate melanoma cells [43]. Nevertheless, it is important to note that the observed association between immune cells and RFS was based on a small cohort, thus these findings were exploratory and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Secondly, our study showed that the combined adjuvant therapy could enhance the diversity of the TCR repertoire, particularly in CD8+ Tem and CD8+ Teff cell populations, in the peripheral blood of patients with resected stage III melanoma. The diversity of the TCR repertoire is a foundational element of successful immunotherapy [44]. It has been reported that high tumor-infiltrating TCR diversity predicts favorable efficacy of PD-1 blockade immunotherapy in patients with metastatic melanoma. High TCR clonal diversity has also been reported to be associated with prolonged survival and a decreased risk of mortality [27, 45]. Increased TCR clonal diversity is a possible mechanism contributing to the enhanced efficacy of combined adjuvant therapy.

Thirdly, our combined adjuvant therapy enhanced the antigen-presenting capacity of naïve B, switched memory B, and unswitched memory B cells. B cells are one of the most prevalent lymphocyte subsets among tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in melanoma. B cells participate in anti-tumor immunity through the production of antibodies and antigen presentation. Furthermore, B cells can indirectly enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy by participating in the formation of tertiary lymphoid structures with T cells and dendritic cells [46, 47]. Moreover, our combined adjuvant therapy also increased BCR clonal diversity. Recently, Che and colleagues [48] reported that effective responses to PD-1 blockade are marked by an increase in BCR clonal diversity following treatment initiation. Increased clonality of the BCR repertoire has been proven to be a favorable prognostic factor in cutaneous melanoma [49].

Fourth, our combined adjuvant therapy increased the proportion of non-classical monocytes and decreased that of classical monocytes. It is well established that classical monocytes secrete VEGF, which promotes tumor cell extravasation and contributes to metastasis. In contrast, non-classical monocytes mediate cytotoxicity of Treg cells and reduce tumor metastasis [50]. A previous study reported that high frequencies of non-classical monocytes are associated with elevated response rates and improved OS in advanced melanoma patients with PD-1 blockade [51]. Furthermore, our combined adjuvant therapy enhanced the antigen-presenting capacity of cDCs, classical monocytes, and non-classical monocytes. After combined adjuvant therapy, cell interactions between myeloid cell subsets and CD8+ T cell subsets were also enhanced. Our combined adjuvant therapy may enhance the immune response to PD-1 blockade by inducing the participation of myeloid cell subsets.

Based on the changes in the peripheral immune landscape described above, we selected two potential biomarkers (NLR and circulating CD8+ Tem) related to therapeutic efficacy and validated them in two independent real-world cohorts of stage III melanoma patients. NLR is a biomarker that can be evaluated through routine blood tests, without requiring specialized equipment or techniques, with the advantages of low cost and easy accessibility in clinical practice. It comprehensively reflects the body’s inflammatory and immune status. Bartlett and colleagues [52] demonstrated that elevated baseline NLR and an early increase of NLR during treatment are associated with treatment failure and predict death in stage IV melanoma patients with PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy. To date, studies assessing the role of NLR in melanoma are mostly limited to metastatic melanoma cases receiving PD-1 inhibitors [52, 53]. To our knowledge, our study suggests that elevated NLR could serve as a cost-effective and readily available biomarker for adverse prognosis in patients with locally advanced melanoma following surgical resection.

In addition, we demonstrated that the level of pretreatment circulating CD8+ Tem might serve as a potential biomarker for the prognosis of patients with resected stage III melanoma undergoing immunotherapy. Circulating CD8+ Tem cells can maintain long-term immunological memory against melanoma tumor antigens. Upon recurrence of melanoma lesions, these memory cells can quickly proliferate and differentiate into CD8+ Teff cells with functional anti-tumor activity [54]. Circulating CD8+ Teff cells subsequently migrate to the tumor site to exert their cytotoxic effects. Consequently, postoperative melanoma patients with higher levels of CD8 + Tem cells in peripheral blood tend to exhibit a recurrence-free survival benefit. Our combined adjuvant therapy led to elevated levels and TCR diversity of CD8+ Tem cells in peripheral circulation, which may represent a possible mechanism contributing to the reduction of recurrence risk.

This study had two limitations. First, this was an exploratory clinical trial, and the results need to be further verified through a well-designed randomized controlled trial to confirm the clinical efficacy and safety of rh-endostatin combined with toripalimab in adjuvant treatment of locally advanced melanoma after surgery. Second, the sample size for sc-RNA sequencing was limited (n = 14) and not sufficient to comprehensively depict the immune heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment. The associations between immune changes and patient prognosis should be considered hypothesis-generating. Future studies should expand the cohort size and integrate single-cell data from tumor tissues and multi-omics approaches (e.g., spatial transcriptomics and proteomics) for systematic analysis.

In conclusion, this prospective trial demonstrated that adjuvant toripalimab (anti-PD-1) combined with rh-endostatin is safe and feasible in Chinese patients with locally advanced melanoma postoperatively, although the primary endpoint was not met. These findings are clinically encouraging, as this combined adjuvant regimen demonstrates potential to augment anti-tumor immunity and mitigate melanoma recurrence risk via multiple complementary mechanistic pathways. These include increased total lymphocyte count; elevated numbers of NK cells, circulating CD8+ Tem cells, and circulating CD8+ Teff cells; increased TCR clonal diversity; improved antigen-presenting capacity of B cells; increased BCR clonal diversity; and a higher number of non-classical monocytes with enhanced antigen-presenting function. Our research provides novel insights into the treatment of Asian patients with locally advanced melanoma.
